newsitem.title: USA: France has no plans for airwave sale - minister.
newsitem.headline: France has no plans for airwave sale - minister.

text.p: The French government currently has no plans to auction its radio airwaves as is now done in the United States, the French minister for post, telecommunications and space, said Wednesday.
"It is not the case at this time," Francois Fillon told an audience at the Center for Security and International Studies.
He said that if spectrum space became scarce because of the number of companies competing for it, then the government would consider an auction system.
A new communications law in France created a new agency for managing the nation's spectrum. Currently, there are seven public organizations in charge of allocating the airwaves.
"It's not the most efficient solution," Fillon said of the existing system.

On another matter, Fillon said the French government would remove its 20 percent cap on foreign ownership in French telecommunications companies if a similar provision were worked out under the current telecom trade talks overseen by the World Trade Organization.

He noted that any dropping of France's investment curb would be automatic in such a case because such a condition is written into the new communications law. The government could also drop its curb on a bilateral basis, if for example the United States were to drop its own foreign ownership restrictions.
